newsitem.title: ESTONIA: GOVERNMENT APPROVES CUSTOMS DUTY LAW PLAN.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT APPROVES CUSTOMS DUTY LAW PLAN.

text.p: Estonia's government on Tuesday approved in principle a plan for customs duty legislation as part of an agricultural support programme although the details of the laws are still to be worked out.

The setting of import tariffs would be a radical move for Estonia, which has so far boasted of its exceptionally open economy. But rural politicians have demanded import tariffs for a long time, saying they need the protection of levies.
"If passed, a customs duty law would establish the order in which tariffs may be established," Agriculture Minister Andres Varik told a news conference.
Varik said there was no decision yet whether the law will define tariff ceilings as well.
A duty law has been discussed only by the parliament's economic commission and the government will discuss the legislation needed at its next session on April 22, Varik added.
"Only one proposal, to establish tariffs on pork, has been made by the government commission," Varik said.
"It needs to be discussed and calculated," he added.
A government commission in March proposed the establishment of 30 to 35 percent tariffs on imported pork and said it was the only agricultural sector, where tariffs may be effective.
